messages:
ashley_support: FYI customer jk reported a spike of 5xxs on /v1/generate-stream and says the client saw a broken pipe + stream stopped mid-response. They claim our metrics are counting their client aborts as backend 5xx. attaching logs they sent.
customer_jk: hitting your hosted API from a node client. after ~12s the stream dies with ECONNRESET, we get a 502 from your gateway and our user sees a partial response. Support told us you count it as a 5xx which is affecting our SLA credits. can you repro?
ashley_support: repro steps from customer attached:
```
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-3b","input":"long streaming test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate-stream
```
They send chunked body and then abort client connection after receiving a few chunks. customer says we return 502 and metrics increment.

michael_sre_oncall: thanks. tagging for SRE. quick q: is this specific to chunked POST bodies or to streaming responses (chunked responses) as well? any request ids from their error page?
customer_jk: they gave this req id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d. response headers we captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: rwd-req-0a1b2c3d
```
No upstream body, just 502 json with "upstream error". our client saw ECONNRESET at the socket level.
jordan_backend: grabbing logs for rwd-req-0a1b2c3d now. initial look shows upstream 'write() failed: Broken pipe' inside runtime output, then gateway (alb/nginx) logged a 502. excerpt:
```
[2025-11-03T15:04:17Z] rwd-req-0a1b2c3d runtime INFO: starting streaming response
[2025-11-03T15:04:29Z] rwd-req-0a1b2c3d runtime ERROR: write failed: Broken pipe (EPIPE)
[2025-11-03T15:04:29Z] rwd-req-0a1b2c3d gateway WARN: upstream prematurely closed connection while streaming
```
This is consistent with client closing socket while we were writing tokens.

michael_sre_oncall: ok that aligns. two things to confirm:
- are we treating write errors that come from downstream/client disconnect as 5xx in aggregated metrics? we should classify them separately (499-like)
- is the gateway returning 502 because it considers the upstream dead? we need to check proxy behavior and status mapping.

jordan_backend: current behavior: runtime raises EPIPE -> runtime returns internal error to the connection handler -> gateway returns 502 to client. We increment route 5xx counters when upstream closes unexpectedly. We do not currently map EPIPE to client-abort.

qa_tester: I can repro locally. steps:
1) start a streaming generate via curl -N
2) after first chunk, run `kill -9` on client to simulate abrupt socket close
Result: runtime logs EPIPE and gateway shows 502. metrics show +1 5xx for route. repro attached.

lina_product: customer hit: "this is causing our error budget to spike" — they want either us to stop counting client aborts as 5xx or give an immediate mitigation. any short-term workaround we can advise them?

michael_sre_oncall: immediate mitigation options:
- customer: use graceful client shutdown (close after receiving final chunk) — not always possible.
- proxy level: increase keepalive/proxy_read_timeout so gateway keeps upstream longer? that won't help if client closed the socket.
- our side: change classification to map EPIPE/client disconnects -> 499-like and do not count toward backend 5xx. low-risk config change.

deply-bot: (system) deploy planned: backend/metrics-classifier v2 -> create ticket
deply-bot: actually deploy-bot: created ticket INF-8142 mapping client disconnects to 499, candidate patch on staging.

jordan_backend: I pushed a staging branch that catches EPIPE/ECONNRESET on write and sets response classification = CLIENT_ABORT. still returns no body to client (can't), but metrics won't increment 5xx. also added log: `client_abort=true` with req id.

qa_tester: tested staging patch:
- simul client kill -> gateway still returns 502 to the captured exiting client (can't change TCP-level), but metrics show CLIENT_ABORT and dashboard 5xx unaffected. added unit + integration tests. patch looks good.

ashley_support: what's timeline to get this to prod? customer is sensitive about SLA impact.

jordan_backend: if SRE gives a +1 we can roll to prod as config-only (metrics classifier) with quick rollback. it's low-risk. will need a canary on a small percentage of traffic, and dashboards to confirm no regressions.

michael_sre_oncall: ok schedule: canary 10% in next deploy window (1h), monitor 5xx/499 rates for 30m, then 100% if stable. I'll own the canary. Jordan, open PR referencing INF-8142 and add feature flag.

jordan_backend: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/infra/metrics-classifier/pulls/92 — includes feature flag `feature.metrics_map_client_abort`. staging tests green.

customer_jk: thanks — will that prevent our SLA credits from being affected retroactively? their legal/ops want to know.

lina_product: we don't retroactively change historical billing, but we can make an exception / credit case — I'll loop legal and billing. need volume numbers.

ashley_support: customer provided metrics: about 120 client-aborts in last 48h on that route, caused 120 5xx increments. Jordan, can we add a temporary alert suppression for this req id pattern or route while we roll?

jordan_backend: added a temporary filter: supress alerts for spikes if `client_abort=true` tag present. note: this doesn't change billing metrics until prod roll. will add a dashboard panel showing client_abort counts.

qa_tester: additional note: this is more frequent when customers use chunked Transfer-Encoding and slow streaming clients (mobile flaky network). we should document recommended client patterns (smaller chunk windows, reconnect strategies) in Support KB.

michael_sre_oncall: agreed. I'll run canary now. monitoring: baseline 5xx=0.9% on route, client_abort tag currently 2.8% in logs.

michael_sre_oncall: canary watch update (T+15m): no increase in 5xx, client_abort tagged events now show up as CLIENT_ABORT in metrics. nothing else anomalous. proceeding to full rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy complete: metrics-classifier v2 -> prod rollout 100% (2025-11-03T16:10:05Z)

jordan_backend: prod notes: when we see `write failed: Broken pipe` we now emit `client_abort=true` and map to CLIENT_ABORT counter. gateway still returns 502/connection reset to the aborting client (expected), but our 5xx aggregates are preserved.

ashley_support: told customer we have a fix rolling out; Lina to handle credits. customer replied:

customer_jk: appreciate the quick turnaround. we'll switch to reconnect logic too but good to have metrics not penalizing us. thanks everyone.

lina_product: opened billing case BL-2231 to review 48h of incidents for credit. keeping thread updated.

qa_tester: follow-ups: add KB article for streaming best practices + add an automated regression test for chunked client aborts to ci.

ashley_support: closing action list:
- Jordan: merge PR, close INF-8142 (in progress)
- Michael: confirm post-deploy monitoring for 24h
- Lina: billing case BL-2231
- QA: KB article + CI test

ashley_support: marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if customer sees further SLA hits.
